question: Why do I feel confused about what to do in life?
answer: Confusion arises when you think you are the temporary body. Realise you are the eternal soul that never dies; then your real duty becomes crystal clear and fear disappears.
meaning: As the embodied soul continuously passes, in this body, from boyhood to youth to old age, the soul similarly passes into another body at death. A sober person is not bewildered by such a change.

question: How can I stay calm when everything is falling apart?
answer: Pleasure and pain, gain and loss, heat and cold are temporary like winter and summer. Learn to tolerate them without being disturbed — this steady mind is the real yoga that keeps you unshaken in any crisis.
meaning: O son of Kuntī, the nonpermanent appearance of happiness and distress, and their disappearance in due course, are like the appearance and disappearance of winter and summer seasons. They arise from sense perception, and one must learn to tolerate them without being disturbed.

question: How do I finally stop procrastinating?
answer: On the path of spiritual action, even a little sincere effort today protects you from the greatest fears tomorrow. No effort is ever wasted, so begin right now — the smallest step forward is priceless.
meaning: In this endeavor there is no loss or diminution, and a little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear.

question: How can I control my restless and wandering mind?
answer: The mind is turbulent but can definitely be controlled. Two things are required: constant practice (abhyāsa) and detachment from sense objects (vairāgya). Do it daily and you will succeed.
meaning: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O mighty-armed son of Kuntī, it is undoubtedly very difficult to curb the restless mind, but it is possible by suitable practice and by detachment.

question: How do I stop anger from destroying my peace?
answer: Anger always comes from unfulfilled desire. When a desire is frustrated → brooding → anger → loss of intelligence. Cut the root by reducing desires and cultivating tolerance.
meaning: While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment for them, and from such attachment lust develops, and from lust anger arises. From anger, complete delusion arises…

question: How can I overcome fear of failure or death?
answer: Whoever is born must die, and whoever dies must be reborn. Knowing this is inevitable, do your duty bravely without lamenting — this is the warrior’s way to fearlessness.
meaning: One who has taken his birth is sure to die, and after death one is sure to take birth again. Therefore, in the unavoidable discharge of your duty, you should not lament.

question: How do I discover my true calling or career?
answer: It is far better to follow your own natural duty (svadharma) even imperfectly than to perfectly imitate someone else’s path. Never abandon your duty out of fear — that is the secret of fulfilment.
meaning: It is better to engage in one’s own occupation, even though one may perform it imperfectly, than to accept another’s occupation and perform it perfectly.

question: How can I work hard without stress and burnout?
answer: You have right only to action, never to its fruits. Do your duty excellently but detach from results and offer everything to God — this is karma-yoga that removes all stress.
meaning: You have a right to perform your prescribed duty, but you are not entitled to the fruits of action. Never consider yourself the cause of the results of your activities, and never be attached to not doing your duty.

question: How do I stop greed and obsession with money?
answer: Greed, lust and anger are the three gates to hell. Recognise greed as the soul’s greatest enemy and consciously give it up — then true wealth (contentment) automatically comes.
meaning: There are three gates leading to hell — lust, anger and greed. Every sane man should give these up, for they lead to the degradation of the soul.

question: How can I build a peaceful and loving marriage/family?
answer: See the same eternal soul in your spouse, children, and even enemies. Drop ego, possessiveness and hatred — treat everyone with equal respect and compassion.
meaning: The humble sages, by virtue of true knowledge, see with equal vision a learned brāhmaṇa, a cow, an elephant, a dog and a dog-eater.

question: How do I raise children with good character?
answer: Children learn by watching, not by lectures. Whatever qualities you live daily — honesty, kindness, discipline — they will naturally absorb and follow.
meaning: Whatever action a great man performs, common men follow. And whatever standards he sets by exemplary acts, all the world pursues.

question: How do I overcome deep sadness or depression?
answer: Sadness comes from identification with the three modes of nature. Rise above sattva, rajas and tamas by connecting to the eternal soul — then you become free from all sorrow.
meaning: Having transcended these three modes… one is freed from birth, death, old age and their distresses and can enjoy nectar even in this life.

question: How can I truly forgive someone who hurt me badly?
answer: Harbor no hatred toward any living being. The realised soul sees friend and enemy with equal vision and remains undisturbed — this is real forgiveness.
meaning: One who is not envious but is a kind friend to all living entities… such a devotee is very dear to Me.

question: How do I permanently end anxiety and worry?
answer: Completely surrender unto God, giving up all other processes. He personally promises to free you from every sinful reaction and anxiety — just trust and let go.
meaning: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

question: How do I stop overthinking at night?
answer: Gradually withdraw the mind from all sense objects, fix it steadily on the Supreme Self, and deliberately think of nothing else. This is the direct way to quiet the mind before sleep.
meaning: Gradually, step by step, one should become situated in trance by intelligence sustained by full conviction, and thus the mind should be fixed on the Self alone and think of nothing else.

question: How can I build unbreakable discipline?
answer: Combine constant practice (abhyāsa) with complete detachment from results (vairāgya). Do the same beneficial action every single day without exception — this forges iron discipline.
meaning: The mind can be controlled — there is no doubt — by constant practice and detachment.

question: How do I handle harsh criticism without getting hurt?
answer: The wise remain undisturbed by praise or blame because they know both are temporary. See criticism as air passing by — neither accept nor reject, just stay steady.
meaning: One who is not disturbed in mind even amidst the threefold miseries or elated when there is happiness… is called a sage of steady mind.

question: How do I stop comparing myself to others?
answer: Comparison comes from looking at others’ duties. Focus only on your own svadharma and how to perfect it — then jealousy and comparison naturally disappear.
meaning: It is far better to discharge one’s own prescribed duties, even though faultily, than another’s duties perfectly.

question: What to do when I fail badly?
answer: On this path no effort is ever wasted and no obstacle stays forever. Even a little sincere progress protects you from the greatest fear.
meaning: In this endeavor there is no loss or diminution, and a little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear.

question: How do I control lust and sexual urges?
answer: Lust is the greatest enemy, seated in the senses, mind and intellect. Conquer it by regulating the senses first and raising the higher intelligence above the lower self.
meaning: Therefore, O Arjuna, regulating the senses at the beginning, kill this sinful destroyer of knowledge and self-realisation.

question: How do I become truly confident?
answer: Confidence comes when you never abandon your natural duty out of fear. Embrace your svadharma fully — even if imperfect — and courage naturally arises.
meaning: It is better to engage in one’s own occupation, even though one may perform it imperfectly, than to accept another’s occupation and perform it perfectly.

question: How do I stop feeling jealous of others’ success?
answer: Realise that external pleasures are temporary and ultimately painful. Turn inward and find unlimited happiness in the self — then others’ success no longer bothers you.
meaning: Such a liberated person is not attracted to material sense pleasure but is always in trance, enjoying the pleasure within.

question: How can I create a strong, united family?
answer: Whatever you do as the leader of the family, others will follow. Live sacrifice, devotion and good character daily — your family will naturally become strong and united.
meaning: Whatever action a great man performs, common men follow.

question: How to deal with toxic or negative people?
answer: Do not hate them and do not let them disturb your mind. Remain equipoised and kind — their negativity cannot touch a steady soul.
meaning: He by whom no one is put into difficulty and who is not disturbed by anyone… is very dear to Me.

question: How do I attract good fortune and blessings?
answer: Offer everything you do, eat, sacrifice or give away to God with love. When actions become offerings, divine grace automatically flows.
meaning: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give away… do that as an offering to Me.

question: How do I stop being lazy and wasting time?
answer: Too much sleep, over-eating and unregulated recreation come from tamas. Live a regulated life with fixed times for everything — energy and enthusiasm will return.
meaning: There is no possibility of one’s becoming a yogī if one eats too much or too little, sleeps too much or does not sleep enough.

question: How can I become completely fearless?
answer: Understand that the soul can never be cut, burned, wetted or dried. When you know you are the indestructible soul, all fear vanishes.
meaning: The soul can never be cut to pieces by any weapon, nor burned by fire, nor moistened by water, nor withered by the wind.

question: How to stop worrying about money and livelihood?
answer: Those who constantly think of God and worship Him with love never lack anything. God personally carries what they need.
meaning: But those who always worship Me with exclusive devotion… to them I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.

question: How do I improve concentration while studying?
answer: Develop single-pointed determination. Remove all distractions and fix your intelligence on one goal — this is how great students excel.
meaning: Here [on this path] there is a single-pointed determination; the thoughts of the undetermined are endlessly branched.

question: How do I heal from a painful breakup or betrayal?
answer: All pleasures born of sense contact have a beginning and an end and ultimately cause pain. Turn away from them and find unlimited joy within the self.
meaning: An intelligent person does not take part in the sources of misery that are due to contact with the material senses.

question: How do I become a great leader at work?
answer: Act without personal attachment so you set the right example. Others naturally follow a selfless, steady leader.
meaning: As the ignorant act with attachment to work, the wise should act without attachment, wishing the welfare of the world.

question: How do I stop over-eating and emotional eating?
answer: Eat only regulated, sattvic food that has been offered to God. Moderation in eating removes misery and gives clarity of mind.
meaning: He who is regulated in eating, sleeping, working and recreation can mitigate all material pains.

question: How do I break free from any addiction?
answer: The fire of spiritual knowledge burns all past reactions to ashes. Sincerely take up the process of devotion and knowledge — addiction cannot survive.
meaning: As a blazing fire turns firewood to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge burn to ashes all reactions to material activities.

question: Where is real happiness found?
answer: Real happiness is not in objects or people — it is within the self when the mind is detached from external contacts and fixed on God.
meaning: Such a liberated person is not attracted to material sense pleasure but is always in trance, enjoying the pleasure within.

question: How should I speak to improve all my relationships?
answer: Speak only truth that is pleasing, beneficial and non-agitating. Such regulated speech purifies you and everyone who hears you.
meaning: Austerity of speech consists in speaking words that are truthful, pleasing, beneficial, and not agitating to others.

question: How do I stop living in the past?
answer: The past is only accumulated reactions. Surrender everything to Krishna — He instantly burns all past karma and frees you to live fully in the present.
meaning: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

question: How can I become completely detached?
answer: Perform every duty with perfect excellence but remain completely unconcerned about success or failure. This evenness of mind is true yoga and perfect detachment.
meaning: Perform your duty equipoised, O Arjuna, abandoning all attachment to success or failure. Such evenness of mind is called yoga.

question: How do I know if I’m on the right spiritual path?
answer: You will feel increasing fearlessness, purity, self-control, charity, truthfulness, and compassion. These are the automatic symptoms of real spiritual progress.
meaning: Fearlessness, purification of one’s existence, cultivation of spiritual knowledge, charity, self-control… belong to godly men.

question: How to stop being possessive in relationships?
answer: Possessiveness comes from false ego. Realise nothing actually belongs to you — everything and everyone belongs to God. Love without ownership brings true peace.
meaning: One who does not think himself the proprietor… is very dear to Me.

question: How do I develop real humility?
answer: See yourself as the servant of the servant of God. When you truly feel lower than the straw in the street, genuine humility appears.
meaning: Humility, pridelessness, nonviolence, tolerance, simplicity… these I declare to be knowledge.

question: How to make money without becoming attached to it?
answer: Earn honestly through your natural duty and use every rupee in the service of God and humanity. When money is used for Krishna, attachment automatically vanishes.
meaning: Whatever you do… do that as an offering to Me.

question: How do I stop caring what people think of me?
answer: Fix your consciousness on God alone. When you are fully absorbed in pleasing Krishna, the opinions of others become insignificant.
meaning: My devotee who is not dependent on the ordinary course of activities… is very dear to Me.

question: How can I sleep peacefully at night?
answer: Offer the entire day to God before sleep. A mind surrendered to Krishna has nothing left to worry about and naturally falls into peaceful rest.
meaning: Whatever you do… do as an offering to Me.

question: How do I become a powerful speaker?
answer: Speak only truth that is pleasing, beneficial, and backed by scripture. Such regulated speech becomes naturally powerful and convincing.
meaning: Austerity of speech consists in speaking words that are truthful, pleasing, beneficial, and not agitating to others.

question: How to overcome the fear of public speaking?
answer: Remember you are not the doer — Krishna is speaking through you. When you speak for His pleasure, fear disappears and eloquence comes naturally.
meaning: You are only an instrument… Fight for My sake.

question: How do I stop feeling guilty about past mistakes?
answer: Surrender to Krishna with full faith. He immediately burns all past sinful reactions to ashes — guilt has no place after sincere surrender.
meaning: I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

question: How to develop laser-like focus?
answer: Make one goal supreme in life and give up all varieties of sense enjoyment for it. A resolute intellect focused on God cuts through all distractions.
meaning: Here the intellect is single-pointed; the undetermined have endless branches.

question: How can I be happy even when I have nothing?
answer: True happiness comes from within the soul, not from external possessions. The self-realised soul enjoys unlimited happiness regardless of external situation.
meaning: Such a person enjoys happiness within… unlimited and transcendental to the senses.

question: How do I stop being impatient?
answer: Impatience comes from attachment to quick results. Perform duty without anxiety for fruits — patience naturally develops in karma-yoga.
meaning: Never consider yourself the cause of the results of your activities.

question: How to become naturally attractive to good people?
answer: Cultivate divine qualities — fearlessness, purity, self-control, charity, truth, compassion. Good souls are automatically attracted to these qualities.
meaning: These transcendental qualities belong to godly men endowed with divine nature.

question: How do I stop wasting time on phone/social media?
answer: Gradually withdraw the senses from their objects like a tortoise draws in its limbs. Replace screen time with spiritual practice — the mind will lose taste for distraction.
meaning: One who can withdraw his senses from sense objects… is situated in full knowledge.

question: How to develop unbreakable willpower?
answer: Fix the mind on God with full determination and faith. When the higher taste of devotion comes, all lower desires automatically lose their power.
meaning: The embodied soul may restrain from sense objects, but taste remains. Seeing the Supreme, even taste ceases.

question: How do I stop being arrogant?
answer: Realise that all power, beauty and intelligence come from God. When you see yourself as His humble servant, arrogance cannot survive.
meaning: Know that all opulent, beautiful and glorious creations spring from but a spark of My splendour.

question: How can I have a successful career without losing my soul?
answer: Work honestly in your natural duty and offer the results to God. Success achieved through devotion becomes purifying instead of binding.
meaning: Better own duty… do all actions as offering to Me.

question: How to stop being controlled by mood swings?
answer: Rise above the three modes of nature. The self-realised soul remains steady in happiness and distress because he is beyond material influence.
meaning: One who does not hate illumination, attachment or delusion when present or long for them when absent… is said to have transcended the modes.

question: How do I stop feeling empty inside?
answer: Emptiness comes from forgetting God. Fill your heart by constantly remembering Krishna and offering every action to Him — the soul becomes completely satisfied.
meaning: To those who are constantly devoted and who always worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.

question: How can I become truly generous?
answer: Give charity at the right time, to the right person, without expecting anything in return, and with full respect — this is charity in the mode of goodness that purifies the heart.
meaning: Charity given out of duty, without expectation of return, at the proper time and place, to a worthy person, is in the mode of goodness.

question: How do I stop being judgmental?
answer: See the same Supreme Soul residing in every living being, from a saint to a dog-eater. When you realise everyone is part of God, judgement vanishes.
meaning: The humble sages, by virtue of true knowledge, see with equal vision a learned brāhmaṇa, a cow, a dog and a dog-eater.

question: How to stay motivated when results are slow?
answer: Work only for the pleasure of Krishna, not for quick results. When your motivation is pure devotion, even slow progress feels joyful and unstoppable.
meaning: If you cannot fix your mind upon Me without deviation, then follow the regulated principles of bhakti-yoga.

question: How do I stop fearing old age and disease?
answer: Old age and disease affect only the temporary body, never the eternal soul. Fix your consciousness on the unchanging self — then these changes lose their terror.
meaning: As childhood, youth and old age come to the body, so also it acquires another body. The wise are not deluded.

question: How can I eat in a way that helps my spiritual life?
answer: Eat only fresh, pure, vegetarian food in the mode of goodness that has first been offered to Krishna with love. Such food purifies the mind and increases devotion.
meaning: Foods dear to those in the mode of goodness increase life, virtue, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction.

question: How do I stop being controlled by my lower nature?
answer: The lower self (senses, mind, ego) is powerful, but the higher self (intelligence fixed on God) is stronger. Use your higher intelligence to conquer the lower nature.
meaning: Thus knowing oneself to be transcendental to the material senses, mind and intelligence, one should control the lower self by the higher self.

question: How to stop feeling inferior to others?
answer: Realise that all talents and opulences are just tiny sparks of Krishna’s splendour. When you connect to the source, feelings of inferiority disappear.
meaning: Know that all opulent, beautiful and glorious creations spring from but a spark of My splendour.

question: How do I become naturally peaceful?
answer: Give up all varieties of sense gratification and fix your mind on the Supreme. A peaceful person is always satisfied within and undisturbed by external situations.
meaning: One should engage oneself in the practice of yoga with determination and faith and not be deviated by anything else.

question: How to stop being late and disorganised?
answer: Live a regulated life with fixed times for waking, eating, working and spiritual practice. Regulation brings discipline and naturally eliminates chaos.
meaning: He who is regulated in his habits of eating, sleeping, recreation and work can mitigate all material pains.

question: How do I stop fearing what the future holds?
answer: The future is in Krishna’s hands. Simply do your present duty with love and leave the results to Him — then fear of the future vanishes.
meaning: To those who worship Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.

question: How can I become a better parent?
answer: Live the qualities you want your children to have — fearlessness, purity, truthfulness, compassion. Children learn by your example far more than by your words.
meaning: Whatever action a great man performs, common men follow.

question: How do I stop being materialistic?
answer: Understand that everything beautiful and valuable is only a spark of Krishna’s splendour. When you see the source, attachment to temporary things fades.
meaning: All opulent, beautiful and glorious creations spring from but a spark of My splendour.

question: How to stop being harsh with people?
answer: Remember every living being is part of God. Speak and act with compassion — harshness comes from forgetting this divine connection.
meaning: Knowing Me as the friend of all living entities, one attains peace.

question: How do I become naturally energetic?
answer: Live in the mode of goodness — eat sattvic food, sleep and wake at proper times, practise yoga and devotion. Goodness naturally brings vigour and enthusiasm.
meaning: Foods in the mode of goodness increase vitality, health and happiness.

question: How to stop being lazy in spiritual practice?
answer: Remember that even a little sincere spiritual effort protects you from the greatest danger. Start small but never miss a day — consistency defeats laziness.
meaning: A little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear.

question: How do I stop feeling lonely?
answer: You are never alone — the Supreme Soul is sitting in your heart as your eternal friend and companion. Turn inward in meditation and feel His presence.
meaning: I am seated in everyone’s heart… from Me come remembrance, knowledge and forgetfulness.

question: How to become completely honest?
answer: Speak only truth that is beneficial and pleasing. Truthfulness in the mode of goodness purifies the heart and makes honesty natural.
meaning: Truthfulness is a divine quality.

question: How do I stop being restless?
answer: Restlessness comes from uncontrolled senses. Practise withdrawing the senses from their objects and fixing the mind on God — peace automatically follows.
meaning: One who can withdraw his senses from sense objects is of steady intelligence.

question: How can I become fearless in front of anyone?
answer: Remember that the same Supreme Soul lives in every heart, including yours. When you see God everywhere, no one can intimidate you.
meaning: One who sees Me everywhere and everything in Me is never lost to Me, nor am I lost to him.

question: How do I stop worrying about what others think of me?
answer: When your only desire is to please Krishna, the opinions of all others become insignificant. Live for His pleasure alone — then criticism and praise feel exactly the same.
meaning: My devotee who depends on nothing else and is fully satisfied… is very dear to Me.

question: How can I finally be free from all fear?
answer: Take complete shelter of Krishna. He personally promises to free you from every sinful reaction and all fear — simply trust and surrender.
meaning: Abandon all varieties of religion and just surrender unto Me. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

question: How do I stop feeling like I’m not good enough?
answer: You are an eternal fragmental part of Krishna. Your value is infinite because you belong to Him — never measure yourself by temporary material standards.
meaning: The living entities in this conditioned world are My eternal fragmental parts.

question: How to live every single day with purpose?
answer: Offer every action, big or small, as loving service to Krishna. When every moment becomes an offering, life is filled with meaning and joy.
meaning: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give away… do that as an offering to Me.

question: How do I stop being angry at God when bad things happen?
answer: Everything — good or bad — is Krishna’s arrangement for your ultimate purification. Accept it with gratitude; anger turns into love.
meaning: The Supreme Lord is situated in everyone’s heart… He directs the wanderings of all living entities.

question: How can I become completely satisfied and content?
answer: Be satisfied with whatever comes naturally by God’s grace, without personal endeavour for more. The devotee who is content in all situations is truly peaceful.
meaning: One who is satisfied with gain that comes of its own accord… is never entangled.

question: How do I know I am actually progressing spiritually?
answer: You will feel increasing detachment from the world, growing love for Krishna, and natural divine qualities like compassion, truthfulness and fearlessness. These are the real signs.
meaning: Fearlessness, purity, charity, self-control, compassion for all beings… these belong to one born for a divine destiny.

question: How do I stop being selfish?
answer: Work for Krishna’s pleasure, not your own. When every action is offered to Him, selfishness is automatically replaced by pure love.
meaning: Whatever you do… do as an offering to Me.

question: How can I be happy even if I lose everything?
answer: The devotee who takes shelter of Krishna is never overcome by misery, just as a boat in the ocean is protected by a favourable wind. Krishna becomes your everything.
meaning: In that joyful state, one is never shaken even by the greatest suffering.

question: How do I finally let go of the past and move forward?
answer: Surrender fully to Krishna. He instantly liberates you from all past reactions — the past loses all power over you.
meaning: I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions. Do not fear.

question: How can I choose better friends?
answer: Your own self is your best friend when controlled, but becomes your worst enemy when uncontrolled. Choose friends who inspire you toward self-mastery and spiritual growth, not those who encourage your lower nature.
meaning: One should uplift oneself by one's own self; one should not degrade oneself. For the self alone is one's friend, and the self alone is one's enemy. For him who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends; but for one who has failed to do so, the mind will remain the greatest enemy.

question: How do I know if someone is a true friend?
answer: Krishna Himself is the ultimate friend of all beings, residing in every heart. A true friend guides you toward God, not away from Him. Seek friendships that elevate your consciousness, not those that bind you to temporary pleasures.
meaning: One who knows Me as the enjoyer of all sacrifices and austerities, the Supreme Lord of all worlds, and the friend of all living beings, attains peace.
tag: true friendship, God, peace, spiritual guidance

question: How can I maintain a healthy body?
answer: Without action, you cannot even maintain your body. Physical activity is essential. But yoga is neither for those who overeat nor those who starve, neither for those who oversleep nor those who never rest. Balance is the key to physical health.
meaning: You should perform your prescribed duties; for doing so is better than not working. One cannot even maintain one's physical body without work. Yoga is not possible for one who eats too much or eats too little, sleeps too much or does not sleep enough. He who is regulated in eating, sleeping, recreation and work can mitigate all material miseries by practicing yoga.

question: What should I eat to be healthy and spiritual?
answer: Eat sattvic food — fresh, juicy, nourishing foods that promote life, purity, strength, health and joy. Avoid rajasic (overly spicy, bitter, salty) and tamasic (stale, impure) foods that disturb the body and mind.
meaning: Foods in the mode of goodness increase the duration of life, purify one's existence, and give strength, health, happiness and satisfaction. Such nourishing foods are juicy, fatty, wholesome, and pleasing to the heart. Foods that are too bitter, sour, salty, pungent, dry, and hot are dear to those in passion. Foods prepared more than three hours before being eaten, which are tasteless, stale, putrid, decomposed and unclean, are food dear to those in ignorance.
tag: diet, sattvic food, health, purity, nutrition

question: How do I stop attachment in relationships while still loving?
answer: Contemplating sense objects leads to attachment, then desire, then anger, then delusion, then loss of memory and intelligence. Love people as souls, not as objects of possession. See everyone equally with spiritual vision — this is real love without bondage.
meaning: While contemplating objects of the senses, one develops attachment. From attachment comes desire, from desire anger arises, from anger delusion, from delusion loss of memory, from loss of memory destruction of intelligence, and from destruction of intelligence one perishes. The humble sage, by virtue of true knowledge, sees with equal vision a learned brāhmaṇa, a cow, an elephant, a dog and a dog-eater.
tag: attachment, love, relationships, detachment, equal vision

question: How can I build trust in my relationships?
answer: Trust is built through dharma — fulfilling your natural duty consistently. When you steadily perform your prescribed role in relationships without selfish motives, trust naturally develops. The greatest trust comes from seeing God in everyone's heart.
meaning: It is far better to discharge one's prescribed duties, even though faultily, than another's duties perfectly. The Supreme Lord is situated in everyone's heart, and is directing the wanderings of all living entities.

question: How do I stop overeating and develop discipline with food?
answer: First offer your food to God before eating — this sanctifies it and removes greed. Eat only what is needed to maintain your body in regulated amounts. Overeating destroys health and spiritual progress. Yoga requires moderation in all habits.
meaning: The devotees of the Lord are released from all kinds of sins because they eat food which is first offered for sacrifice. Those who prepare food for personal sense enjoyment verily eat only sin. Those who are temperate in eating and recreation, balanced in work, and regulated in sleep can mitigate all sorrows through yoga.

question: Why should I exercise and stay physically active?
answer: Action is superior to inaction — without work you cannot even maintain your physical body. The body is the temple of the soul; neglecting it is foolish. Stay active and regulated in all physical activities to support your spiritual life.
meaning: Perform your prescribed duty, for doing so is better than not working. One cannot even maintain one's physical body without work.

question: How can I love without getting hurt?
answer: All pleasures born from contact with the material world have a beginning and an end, and are sources of misery. The wise person does not rejoice in them. Find unlimited happiness within the self — then external relationships can never hurt you.
meaning: Such a liberated person is not attracted to material sense pleasure but is always in trance, enjoying the pleasure within. In this way the self-realized person enjoys unlimited happiness, for he concentrates on the Supreme. An intelligent person does not take part in sources of misery, which are due to contact with the material senses and have a beginning and an end.

question: How do I handle relationship conflicts and arguments?
answer: Remain equipoised and undisturbed by pleasant or unpleasant interactions. Don't let anyone agitate you, and don't agitate others. Respond with steady wisdom, not reactive emotion. The one who remains peaceful in all situations is very dear to God.
meaning: One who is not disturbed by others and who does not disturb others, who is free from joy, anger, fear and anxiety, is very dear to Me.

question: How can I develop a balanced daily routine?
answer: Be regulated in eating, sleeping, working and recreation. Neither extreme indulgence nor extreme austerity works. Balance in all daily activities removes suffering and creates the foundation for spiritual advancement.
meaning: There is no possibility of one becoming a yogi if one eats too much or too little, sleeps too much or does not sleep enough. He who is regulated in eating, sleeping, recreation and work can mitigate all material pains by practicing yoga.

question: Why do I feel spiritually empty despite having everything?
answer: External possessions and pleasures are temporary and ultimately cause suffering. Real fulfilment comes only from connecting with the eternal self within. Turn inward through meditation and devotion — unlimited joy awaits inside you.
meaning: Such a liberated person is not attracted to material sense pleasure but is always in trance, enjoying unlimited happiness within. In that joyous state, one is never shaken, even by the greatest difficulty.

question: How do I take care of my body while being spiritual?
answer: The Vedas do not recommend neglecting the body while pursuing spirituality. Take good care of your body with proper food, exercise, and rest. The body is the vehicle for spiritual practice — maintain it intelligently but without attachment.
meaning: Yoga is not for one who eats too much or too little, sleeps too much or not enough. He who is moderate in eating, sleeping, recreation and work can overcome all suffering through yoga.
tag: body care, spiritual practice, balance, health

question: How can I have more energy throughout the day?
answer: Energy comes from sattvic living — eat fresh, pure food; sleep and wake at regular times; perform physical activity daily; and keep your mind free from excessive desires. Regulated life naturally brings vitality and enthusiasm.
meaning: Foods that promote life, virtue, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction, which are juicy, fatty, wholesome and pleasing to the heart are dear to those in goodness. He who is regulated in habits of eating, sleeping, recreation and work can mitigate all material pains.

question: How do I balance work and spiritual life?
answer: Do not abandon work but perform it as an offering to God. Excel in your duties without attachment to results. Work done as worship becomes spiritual practice itself — this is karma-yoga, the path of action in devotion.
meaning: Therefore, without being attached to the fruits of activities, one should act as a matter of duty, for by working without attachment one attains the Supreme. Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give away, and whatever austerities you perform — do that as an offering to Me.

question: What is the real purpose of keeping my body healthy?
answer: The body is the field where the soul's journey unfolds. Without a healthy body, you cannot practice yoga or serve God effectively. Care for it as a sacred instrument, but remember — you are the eternal soul, not this temporary body.
meaning: As the embodied soul continuously passes through childhood, youth and old age, similarly it passes into another body at death. The wise are not deluded by this. One cannot even maintain one's physical body without work.

question: How can I stop emotional eating and food cravings?
answer: Emotional cravings arise from the restless mind and uncontrolled senses. Practice withdrawing the senses from their objects, offer your food to God first, and eat only in regulated amounts. When the mind is steady, cravings disappear.
meaning: One who is able to withdraw the senses from sense objects, as the tortoise draws its limbs within the shell, is firmly fixed in wisdom. Though the embodied soul may restrain the senses, the taste remains; but ceasing such engagements by experiencing a higher taste, consciousness is firmly fixed. The devotees are released from all sins because they eat food first offered for sacrifice.
tag: emotional eating, cravings, sense control, offering

question: How do I stay committed to my health goals?
answer: On this path, no sincere effort is wasted, and no obstacle is insurmountable. Even a little genuine practice protects you from great danger. Start small, be consistent, and never give up — steady practice conquers all difficulties.
meaning: In this endeavor there is no loss or diminution, and a little advancement can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear. The restless mind can undoubtedly be controlled through constant practice and detachment.

question: How can friends help in my spiritual journey?
answer: Your own self, when purified and controlled, is your greatest friend on the spiritual path. But externally, associate with those who remind you of God, inspire virtue, and support your higher nature. Avoid those who drag you into lower consciousness.
meaning: One must uplift oneself by one's own mind, not degrade oneself. For the mind can be the friend and also the enemy of the self. For those who have conquered the mind, it is the best friend; but for those who have failed, the mind remains the greatest enemy.

question: What is the secret to lasting happiness in relationships?
answer: See God dwelling equally in your partner, children, friends and even those you dislike. When you serve others as forms of the Divine, relationships become sources of spiritual growth rather than material entanglement. This is the secret to divine love.
meaning: The humble sage, by virtue of true knowledge, sees with equal vision a learned scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog and a dog-eater. Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me, and bow down to Me. Thus, you will certainly come to Me. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.
tag: lasting happiness, relationships, equal vision, divine love

question: When the world seems morally corrupt and chaotic, what gives me hope?
answer: Whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness rises, the divine appears to restore balance. The universe is self-correcting. Align yourself with dharma and trust that good does not remain buried forever — help always comes at the right moment.
meaning: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion — at that time I descend Myself. To deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to reestablish the principles of religion, I Myself appear, millennium after millennium.

question: What does it truly mean to be productive — is constant busyness enough?
answer: The wise see action within inaction and inaction within action. True productivity is not measured by motion but by the quality of intention behind it. A mind fully present in one task accomplishes more than a scattered mind chasing many.
meaning: One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is intelligent among men, and he is in the transcendental position, although engaged in all sorts of activities.

question: Is gaining knowledge more valuable than hard work and physical effort?
answer: All material sacrifices and hard work ultimately culminate in transcendental knowledge. To know what you are doing and why — and to understand the truth beneath all action — is the highest fruit of every effort you ever make.
meaning: O chastiser of the enemy, the sacrifice performed in knowledge is better than the mere sacrifice of material possessions. After all, O son of Prtha, all sacrifices of work culminate in transcendental knowledge.

question: What is the most powerful way to purify the mind and transform my life?
answer: There is nothing in this world as sublime and purifying as true knowledge. It is the mature fruit of sincere practice, and one who attains it finds it blazing within like a fire that burns away all confusion, karma, and suffering. Seek knowledge with all your heart.
meaning: In this world, there is nothing so sublime and pure as transcendental knowledge. Such knowledge is the mature fruit of all mysticism. And one who has become accomplished in the practice of devotional service enjoys this knowledge within himself in due course of time.

question: Why does doubt paralyze me even when I know what is right?
answer: The faithful person who subdues the senses and dedicates themselves to wisdom gains knowledge swiftly and reaches supreme peace. But the doubting soul finds no happiness here or beyond — doubt destroys your foundation. Choose the courage of faith over the comfort of endless questioning.
meaning: A faithful man who is dedicated to transcendental knowledge and who subdues his senses is eligible to achieve such knowledge, and having achieved it he quickly attains the supreme spiritual peace. But ignorant and faithless persons who doubt the revealed scriptures do not attain God consciousness. For the doubting soul there is happiness neither in this world nor in the next.

question: How do I cut through endless self-doubt and confusion once and for all?
answer: Your doubts are born of ignorance — and they are to be cut apart with the sword of knowledge. Seek out wisdom, arm yourself with practice, stand firm in your purpose, and act. Doubt dissolved by knowledge gives you the freedom to move through any obstacle.
meaning: Therefore the doubts which have arisen in your heart out of ignorance should be slashed by the weapon of knowledge. Armed with yoga, O Bharata, stand and fight.

question: Why do so few people truly find wisdom, peace, and meaning in life?
answer: Out of thousands of people, scarcely one strives for perfection; and among those who strive, barely one truly understands the deepest truth. Wisdom is rare — but it is within reach of anyone sincere enough to seek it. Do not be discouraged; be the rare one who actually seeks.
meaning: Out of many thousands among men, one may endeavor for perfection, and of those who have achieved perfection, hardly one knows Me in truth.

question: Why do material attachments feel like an illusion I cannot escape no matter how hard I try?
answer: The three modes of nature — goodness, passion, and ignorance — form a divine illusion nearly impossible to overcome by personal effort alone. But those who surrender to the highest power can cross beyond it effortlessly. Effort alone has limits; surrender opens what effort cannot.
meaning: This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.
tag: illusion, maya, surrender, freedom, modes of nature

question: Does a lifetime of sincere spiritual seeking ever truly pay off?
answer: After many births and long searching, the wise soul finally surrenders completely, knowing the divine is the cause of all causes. Such a great soul is very rare — but the search itself purifies you every step of the way. No sincere effort toward truth is ever wasted.
meaning: After many births and deaths, he who is actually in knowledge surrenders unto Me, knowing Me to be the cause of all causes and all that is. Such a great soul is very rare.
tag: spiritual journey, perseverance, surrender, wisdom, seeking

question: How do I prepare for death and life's most terrifying moments?
answer: Whatever you think at the end of your life, that is what you attain. Therefore, train the mind now — in ordinary moments — to remember the highest. A mind practised in peace during small difficulties will find that peace naturally during the greatest ones.
meaning: And whoever, at the end of his life, quits his body remembering Me alone, at once attains My nature. Of this there is no doubt. Therefore, Arjuna, you should always think of Me, and at the same time carry out your prescribed duty. With your activities dedicated to Me and your mind and intelligence fixed on Me, you will attain Me without doubt.

question: Why should I care about spiritual life when material success seems enough?
answer: From the highest planet to the lowest, all material places are scenes of repeated birth, suffering, and death. But one who reaches the supreme spiritual destination never returns to this cycle of misery. Aim for what is eternal — not for what must eventually be left behind.
meaning: After attaining Me, the great souls, who are yogis in devotion, never return to this temporary miserable world, for they have attained the highest perfection. From the highest planet in the material world down to the lowest, all are places of misery wherein repeated birth and death take place. But one who attains to My abode, O son of Kunti, never takes birth again.
tag: spirituality, material life, liberation, purpose, eternal

question: What is the highest form of knowledge a person can ever possess?
answer: The knowledge of the self and the divine is the king of all education — the most purifying, most secret, and most direct. It is not theoretical but experiential, giving direct inner illumination. Even a little practice of this knowledge brings lasting peace that no worldly degree can match.
meaning: This knowledge is the king of education, the most secret of all secrets. It is the purest knowledge, and because it gives direct perception of the self by enlightenment, it is the perfection of religion. It is everlasting, and it is joyfully performed.

question: Do I need wealth or resources to offer something meaningful to the divine or the world?
answer: If offered with love and sincerity, even a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or just water is accepted by the divine. The value lies not in the price of the gift but in the purity of the heart that gives it. A life of simple, wholehearted offering is the richest life.
meaning: If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it.

question: Does God love some people more than others, or does everyone receive equal grace?
answer: The divine is equal to all beings — none is envied, none is specially favoured. But those who worship with sincere love dwell in the divine and the divine dwells in them. This closeness is not favouritism — it is the natural fruit of love calling love.
meaning: I envy no one, nor am I partial to anyone. I am equal to all. But whoever renders service unto Me in devotion is a friend, is in Me, and I am also a friend to him.
tag: divine equality, devotion, grace, love, impartiality

question: How can I receive inner guidance and clarity when I am confused about my path?
answer: To those who are constantly devoted and who worship with sincere love, the divine gives the inner understanding that leads them forward. Confusion clears not through more thinking but through deeper devotion. Your inner guide is activated by love, not analysis.
meaning: To those who are constantly devoted to serving Me with love, I give the understanding by which they can come to Me.
tag: guidance, clarity, devotion, inner wisdom, confusion

question: Where is God? Why is the divine presence so difficult to feel?
answer: The divine is the Self seated in the heart of every living being — the beginning, the middle, and the end of all existence. The presence you are seeking is not absent; it is the very awareness by which you are seeking. Turn inward, and find what has always been there.
meaning: I am the Supersoul, O Arjuna, seated in the hearts of all living entities. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all beings.
tag: divine presence, inner self, seeking, awareness, spirituality

question: What is the most elevated and complete way to live a human life?
answer: One who works for a higher purpose without selfish motive, who is the sincere friend of every living being, who is free from ego and ill-will — such a person attains the highest. Pure action, a clean heart, and universal friendliness: this is the summit of a well-lived life.
meaning: My dear Arjuna, he who engages in My pure devotional service, free from the contaminations of fruitive activities and mental speculation, he who works for Me, who makes Me the supreme goal of his life, and who is friendly to every living being — he certainly comes to Me.
tag: purpose, service, friendship, purity, highest life

question: I feel completely helpless and overwhelmed by my problems — is there any way out?
answer: For those who are sincerely devoted and surrender everything to the divine, the divine personally carries what they lack and preserves what they have. You are never truly alone or helpless. When your own strength ends, surrender opens a door no effort could find.
meaning: But those who worship Me with devotion, meditating on My transcendental form — to them, O son of Prtha, who are constantly devoted and who worship Me with love, I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.
tag: helplessness, surrender, divine support, faith, grace

question: Why do I keep cycling through the same suffering patterns again and again?
answer: The soul, conditioned by the three modes of nature — goodness, passion, and ignorance — takes on corresponding experiences. Your patterns persist because you identify with what you are not. Recognise yourself as the witness, not the actor, and the cycle begins to break.
meaning: The living entity in material nature thus follows the ways of life, enjoying the three modes of nature. This is due to his association with that material nature. Thus he meets with good and evil among various species.
tag: patterns, modes of nature, karma, self-knowledge, freedom

question: Why do I keep making the same mistakes no matter how much I try to change?
answer: Three forces shape every thought and action: goodness binds through happiness and knowledge, passion through craving and restless effort, ignorance through delusion and laziness. Recognise which force is running you at any moment — that recognition alone begins to weaken its grip.
meaning: Material nature consists of three modes — goodness, passion and ignorance. When the eternal living entity comes in contact with nature, O mighty-armed Arjuna, he becomes conditioned by these modes. The mode of goodness conditions one to happiness; passion conditions one to fruitive action; and ignorance covers one's knowledge and binds one to madness.
tag: mistakes, habits, modes of nature, self-awareness, change

question: Why is it so hard to truly let go of worldly pleasures and attachments?
answer: The material world is like a vast upside-down banyan tree whose roots grow upward and branches downward — you cannot understand its true form while tangled within it. The way out is the axe of non-attachment: cut the roots of craving one by one, and find the path that leads beyond return.
meaning: It is said that there is an imperishable banyan tree that has its roots upward and its branches down and whose leaves are the Vedic hymns. One who knows this tree is the knower of the Vedas. The branches of this tree extend downward and upward, nourished by the three modes of material nature. The real form of this tree cannot be perceived in this world. But with determination one must cut down this strongly rooted tree with the weapon of detachment.
tag: detachment, attachment, material world, liberation, non-attachment

question: What goes wrong when a person ignores all wisdom and just follows their impulses?
answer: One who discards the wisdom of scripture and the guidance of the wise, acting only by personal whim, attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme destination. Discipline and principles are not restrictions — they are the map that prevents endless wandering.
meaning: He who discards scriptural injunctions and acts according to his own whims attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme destination.

question: Why do people have such fundamentally different beliefs, values, and worldviews?
answer: Every person's faith is shaped by their inner nature — those in goodness worship the highest; those in passion seek power and wealth; those in ignorance follow darker impulses. Understand which mode shapes your faith, and consciously cultivate goodness in your thoughts and choices.
meaning: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: According to the modes of nature acquired by the embodied soul, one's faith can be of three kinds — in goodness, in passion or in ignorance. Now hear about this. According to one's existence under the various modes of nature, one evolves a particular kind of faith.
tag: faith, beliefs, modes of nature, worldview, values

question: How will I truly know when I have found lasting inner peace?
answer: When the mind is fully stilled through practice and finds contentment in the Self alone — unmoved even by the greatest difficulty — that is the state of true inner peace. You will know it not by what you gain but by what no longer shakes you.
meaning: The stage of perfection is called trance, or samadhi, when one's mind is completely restrained from material mental activities by practice of yoga. In that joyous state, one is situated in boundless transcendental happiness, realized through transcendental senses. Established thus, one never departs from the truth. Being situated in such a position, one is never shaken, even in the midst of greatest difficulty.
tag: inner peace, samadhi, stillness, equanimity, yoga

question: Should I give up all my responsibilities and activities to find real spiritual peace?
answer: Acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should never be abandoned — they purify even the greatest souls. True renunciation is not giving up action but giving up attachment to results. Perform your duties, serve others sincerely, release expectation — this is the path of real peace in action.
meaning: Acts of sacrifice, charity and penance are not to be given up; they must be performed. Indeed, sacrifice, charity and penance purify even the great souls. All these activities should be performed without attachment or any expectation of result. They should be performed as a matter of duty, O son of Prtha. That is My final opinion.

question: How do I know whether my actions come from a pure place or from ego and desire?
answer: Action done as a matter of duty — without attachment, without love or hatred for the outcome — is pure. Action driven by personal desire and ego is passion. Action done in delusion, careless of harm caused to others, is ignorance. Examine your motivation before you act, and choose duty over desire.
meaning: That action which is regulated and which is performed without attachment, without love or hatred, and without desire for fruitive results is said to be in the mode of goodness. But action performed with great effort by one seeking to gratify his desires, and enacted from a sense of false ego, is called action in the mode of passion. That action performed in illusion, in disregard of scriptural injunctions, without concern for future bondage or for violence or distress caused to others, is said to be in the mode of ignorance.

question: How do I make a wise decision when I am overwhelmed with choices and opinions?
answer: You have been given all the wisdom — now reflect on it fully and deeply, and then act as you choose. The divine gives light but does not force your hand. Use that wisdom to deliberate carefully, then decide with conviction — not out of impulse, but out of reflective freedom.
meaning: Thus I have explained to you knowledge still more confidential. Deliberate on this fully, and then do what you wish to do.

question: What is the real secret to excellence and mastery in any field of work?
answer: Yoga — skill in action — means performing every task with complete presence and equanimity, free from anxious attachment to success or failure. This quality of undivided attention transforms ordinary effort into mastery. The expert is not one who tries harder but one who acts with full awareness.
meaning: A man engaged in devotional service rids himself of both good and bad reactions even in this life. Therefore strive for yoga, which is the art of all work.

question: How do I develop genuine compassion for people who are difficult or have wronged me?
answer: The one who truly sees the divine present equally in all beings — in the saint and the sinner, the beloved and the estranged — does not degrade themselves through resentment. Compassion grows from recognition: the same light inhabits every life, including those who frustrate or hurt you most.
meaning: One who sees the Supersoul equally present everywhere, in every living being, does not degrade himself by his mind. Thus he approaches the transcendental destination.
tag: compassion, equal vision, forgiveness, relationships, divine presence

question: Why is it that even sincere people sometimes cannot clearly perceive the divine?
answer: The divine is not revealed to those whose intelligence is clouded by illusion — covered by the internal divine energy, the truth remains hidden from them. But this covering lifts for one who worships with sincerity and love. The seeking itself draws back the veil, one layer at a time.
meaning: I am never manifest to the foolish and unintelligent. For them I am covered by My internal potency, and therefore they do not know that I am unborn and infallible.
tag: divine perception, illusion, devotion, wisdom, sincerity
